brief: Two-storey commercial building of 1848 built of fieldstone/cobble masonry with dressed stone quoins at the corners, three upper 6/6 windows, a plain boxed cornice and a small parapet; the shopfront has two big multi-pane windows either side of a recessed door and a signboard reading 'PALMYRA ENTERPRISE' - it housed the village newspaper. HABS drawings record plans and elevations.

facade.notes: the Enterprise Building (Palmyra WI, 1848): a two-storey front of cobblestone fieldstone with dressed quoins and lintels, a stone parapet, a symmetrical storefront with a recessed entry and wooden frames; the newspaper's sign 'PALMYRA ENTERPRISE'

why.note: the two-part block: shop below, lodge hall or flats above
cobblestone masonry: rounded field stones laid in courses, a western-New-York craft carried to Wisconsin
